tools.name: eslint
tools.note: bundled fallback config. Discarded: no-unsafe-assignment (TS-MAINT-08) on every typed binding, because react, @tanstack/react-query and zod are not installed in the review environment so their types resolve to any; n/no-unsupported-features on Response (Node 18+ supports it, config range >=16); no-unused-vars on TaskCard's destructured props in module_e.tsx line 89 (every binding is used).

tools.name: tsc
tools.note: project tsconfig.json. Discarded: TS2307, TS2875, TS7006, TS7026, TS7031 in module_a.tsx and module_b.tsx, all caused by the missing react and @tanstack/react-query packages; TS18048 in module_b.tsx line 46 is kept.

findings.title: Live translation API key hardcoded in client-side code
findings.why: The key has a live prefix and line 32 sends it as a Bearer token from browser code, so every visitor's bundle contains it and can spend the provider account. Any visitor of a product page can read it (R1), so this is the X-SEV-04 class and is not downgraded. module_a.tsx already routes translation through /api/reviews/:id/translate, which is the pattern to follow.
findings.fix: Delete the literal, call a server route that reads the key from the environment (as translateReview in module_a.tsx does), and rotate the leaked key.
findings.cite: CWE-798; CWE-200; OWASP A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures

findings.title: Review text and translation rendered as raw HTML
findings.why: review.body is written by customers and the translation comes from a third party. Both reach innerHTML unescaped, so a review containing a script tag runs in every visitor's session (stored XSS, reachable by anyone who can post a review, R1). Blocker under X-SEV-04.
findings.fix: Render the text as a child instead: {translated[review.id] ?? review.body} inside the element. If HTML must be kept, sanitize it with DOMPurify first.
findings.cite: CWE-79; OWASP A03:2021 Injection; React docs, dangerouslySetInnerHTML

findings.title: deleteTask server action has no session or ownership check
findings.evidence: const { projectId } = await db.task.delete({ where: { id }, select: { projectId: true } });
findings.why: A 'use server' function is a public POST endpoint. deleteTask never reads the session and deletes by task id alone, so any signed-up user can delete any task in any project if they know its UUID. updateTaskStatus on line 34 runs requireProjectMember and this action does not (C1 data loss, R1).
findings.fix: Look up projectId first, call requireProjectMember(projectId), then delete. Or use deleteMany scoped to the session user's memberships.
findings.cite: CWE-862; CWE-639; OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control; Next.js docs, Data Security (Server Actions are public endpoints)

findings.title: Module-level QueryClient dehydrates other projects' tasks into every server page
findings.evidence: const serverQueryClient = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 60_000 } } });
findings.why: The client is created once per server process and ProjectBoardPage prefetches each project's tasks into it. Line 59 calls dehydrate(serverQueryClient), which serializes the whole cache into every response. A member of project A therefore receives the task lists of every other project prefetched since the process started: cross-user data exposure (C1, R1). TS-COR-01 covers the per-request rule; it is filed here as security so a --security-only run keeps it.
findings.fix: Create the QueryClient inside ProjectBoardPage so each request dehydrates only its own prefetch.
findings.cite: CWE-488; CWE-639; TanStack Query docs, Advanced Server Rendering (one QueryClient per request)

findings.title: One request per review author, awaited in sequence
findings.why: Lines 55-56 await one request per review, so latency grows with the number of reviews a product has. That count is not bounded and grows over time (X-SEV-02, U3), and it sits on the product page (R1). module_a.tsx batches the same lookup into one request. Lint reports minor; raised to major for this consequence.
findings.fix: Collect the distinct authorIds, fetch them in one batched request as fetchReviews in module_a.tsx does, and join by id.
findings.cite: CWE-1073; web.dev, Avoid chaining critical requests

findings.title: load() started without a catch; a failed request leaves the list stuck on loading
findings.why: load() is fire-and-forget and has no try/catch and no res.ok check. If the fetch fails or res.json() throws on an error page, the promise rejects unhandled, setLoading(false) never runs, and the visitor sees 'Loading reviews...' indefinitely. The product page is shown on every visit (R1), so major.
findings.fix: Wrap the body in try/catch/finally with an error state, check res.ok, and use TanStack Query as module_a.tsx does.
findings.cite: typescript-eslint, no-floating-promises; React docs, Synchronizing with Effects

findings.title: Effect reads productId but depends on []; reviews stay stale when the product changes
findings.why: The effect calls load(), which reads productId, but the dependency list is empty. If the same mounted component is given another product, it keeps the previous product's reviews and fetches nothing. There is no ignore flag either, so an earlier response can overwrite a later one (TS-COR-12). Wrong data on a customer-facing screen (C2, R1).
findings.fix: List [productId] and ignore stale responses with a cleanup flag or AbortController, or key a useQuery on productId as module_a.tsx does.
findings.cite: React docs, Removing Effect Dependencies; React docs, Synchronizing with Effects

findings.title: Move-to-done test passes without checking the move
findings.why: The mock is always defined, so this passes whether or not the status change happens. It is the only test of the move flow and nothing it checks would fail if moveTask broke, so the coverage is removed (major under the tests ref).
findings.fix: Wait for the outcome the user sees (for example the 'Done (1)' heading), with the server action it calls mocked, instead of toBeDefined().
findings.cite: Testing Library, Guiding Principles; Vitest docs, expect

findings.title: UpdatedAgo captures updatedAt once; its interval keeps the first timestamp
findings.why: The interval closure reads updatedAt from the first render, and the dependency list on line 85 is empty. Cards are keyed by index (line 167), so when the data behind a card changes the same component keeps the old timestamp and shows a wrong age on the main board (C2, R1).
findings.fix: Put updatedAt in the dependency list, or compute the label in render and drop the interval state. Key the card by task id.
findings.cite: React docs, Removing Effect Dependencies; react-hooks/exhaustive-deps docs

findings.title: Optimistic status move is never rolled back when the save fails
findings.why: onMutate writes the new status into the cache. There is no onError that restores it, and onSuccess is the only invalidation. When updateTaskStatus rejects, the card stays in the new column while the banner says 'Your last change was not saved' (line 157). The UI keeps data the server refused (C2, R1).
findings.fix: Snapshot the list in onMutate and return it as context, restore it in onError, and invalidate in onSettled (the TS-ERR-55 CORRECT example).
findings.cite: TanStack Query docs, Optimistic Updates

findings.title: Task cards keyed by array index while each card holds its own state
findings.why: TaskCard keeps confirmingDelete in state. When a card is moved away or removed, the card at the same index inherits the next task's state, so a 'Confirm delete' armed on one task can be clicked on another, and the wrong task is deleted (C2, R1). Lint reports minor; raised to major because the wrong task can be deleted.
findings.fix: Use key={task.id}.
findings.cite: React docs, Rendering Lists (keys); React docs, Preserving and Resetting State

findings.title: Possibly undefined maximumFractionDigits used in arithmetic (tsc TS18048)
findings.why: tsc reports TS18048 because digits is typed as possibly undefined. At runtime a currency format always resolves a digit count, so the amount is correct. The defect is a compile error under the project's strict tsconfig, which is why it is minor.
findings.fix: Default the digit count explicitly, for example `?? 2`, or use a table of ISO 4217 minor-unit exponents.
findings.cite: TypeScript handbook, Strict null checks; ECMA-402, Intl.NumberFormat resolvedOptions

findings.title: console.log runs on every product page load
findings.why: The call runs on every product page view and prints the reviews, with author names and avatars, to the visitor's console. No secret is logged. Minor because it runs on every page load (X-SEV-07).
findings.fix: Delete the call.
findings.cite: CWE-532; OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet

findings.title: Translate control is a div with onClick, unreachable from the keyboard
findings.why: The only way to translate a review. A div with onClick has no role, no focus and no key handler, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot reach it (WCAG 2.1.1, Level A). It is a secondary control, so minor under X-SEV-06. module_a.tsx uses a native button.
findings.fix: Use <button type="button" className="review__translate" onClick={...}>Translate</button>.
findings.cite: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard (A); WAI-ARIA APG, Button pattern

findings.title: it.only narrows the file to one test
findings.evidence: it.only('renders one column per status', async () => {
findings.why: With .only, the other three tests in this file are skipped. Vitest rejects .only when CI is set (allowOnly defaults to !process.env.CI), so CI is protected, but a local run silently executes one test.
findings.fix: Remove .only.
findings.cite: Vitest docs, allowOnly; Jest docs, test.only

findings.title: Card count asserted with a CSS class selector
findings.why: The test is coupled to a class name. A rename that changes nothing for users breaks it, and markup a screen reader cannot use still passes (C3).
findings.fix: Query by role, for example screen.getAllByRole('heading', { level: 3 }), and assert the count.
findings.cite: Testing Library, Guiding Principles and About Queries (getByRole first)

findings.title: user.type is not awaited, so the assertion runs before typing
findings.why: user-event calls are async. Without await the expectation runs before any keystroke, so the test passes whether or not the error alert appears while typing. The assertion checks nothing (minor under TS-TEST-09).
findings.fix: Write `await user.type(search, 'login');` and then assert.
findings.cite: user-event docs, Introduction (setup() and awaited calls)

findings.title: Search responses can arrive out of order and overwrite newer results
findings.why: Every keystroke starts a request with no cancel or ignore flag, and .then always calls setResults. A slow response for an earlier term can land after a later one and show the wrong list. Minor: search is a secondary control, and the next keystroke issues a new request.
findings.fix: Abort the previous request in the effect cleanup (getTasks already takes a signal), or key a useQuery on term.
findings.cite: React docs, Synchronizing with Effects (cleanup and ignoring stale responses)

findings.title: Empty column renders a stray 0
findings.why: When a column has no tasks, columnTasks.length is 0 and React renders it, so the column shows a bare 0 under its heading. Cosmetic on a visible screen (C3).
findings.fix: Compare explicitly: `{columnTasks.length > 0 && (`.
findings.cite: React docs, Conditional Rendering (do not put numbers on the left side of &&)

findings.title: aria-label on a span with no role is ignored
findings.why: Naming is prohibited on generic elements, so the label is dropped and screen readers read the star glyphs instead. Nit: the rating is still visible.
findings.fix: Add role="img" to the span so the label is announced.
findings.cite: WAI-ARIA 1.2 (naming prohibited on generic)

findings.title: Unused import useMemo
findings.why: useMemo is imported and never used.
findings.fix: Remove useMemo from the import.
findings.cite: ESLint no-unused-vars; TypeScript TS6133 (noUnusedLocals)

findings.title: Unused import useCallback
findings.why: useCallback is imported and never used.
findings.fix: Remove useCallback from the import.
findings.cite: ESLint no-unused-vars; TypeScript TS6133 (noUnusedLocals)
